preventive_measures: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn to eliminate overwintering fungal ascospores.
Prune dense canopies during dormancy to improve sunlight penetration and air movement.
Apply protective sulfur or copper-based sprays during the green-tip bud stage.
Apple___Apple_scab.treatment_summary: Apply captan or myclobutanil early in the infection cycle. Maintain leaf dryness through drip irrigation.

Apple___Black_rot.disease_name: Apple Black Rot / Frogeye Leaf Spot (Botryosphaeria obtusa)
preventive_measures: Prune out dead wood, fire blight cankers, and mummified fruit lingering on trees.
Disinfect pruning tools with 70% isopropyl alcohol between branch cuts.
Avoid tree mechanical stress and insect wounds during summer.
Apple___Black_rot.treatment_summary: Apply thiophanate-methyl or captan starting at petal fall through cover sprays.

preventive_measures: Remove nearby eastern red cedar and juniper hosts within 1-2 miles if possible.
Select resistant apple rootstocks (e.g., Enterprise, Freedom, Liberty).
Inspect nearby junipers in spring for gelatinous orange spore horns.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.treatment_summary: Spray preventative fungicides (myclobutanil or mancozeb) when apple buds show pink.

preventive_measures: Continue balanced N-P-K fertilization and seasonal soil organic mulching.
Conduct regular scouting for early signs of codling moth and foliar spotting.
Maintain consistent soil moisture levels with automated drip irrigation.
Apple___Healthy.treatment_summary: No curative treatment required. Maintain standard cultural orchard practices.

preventive_measures: Plant only certified disease-free, hot-water treated seeds or resistant cultivars.
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation that splashes bacteria across adjacent foliage.
Rotate fields away from solanaceous crops (peppers, tomatoes, eggplants) for at least 2 years.
Bell_Pepper___Bacterial_spot.treatment_summary: Apply fixed copper bactericides combined with mancozeb upon initial spot detection.

preventive_measures: Maintain raised beds with organic mulch to stabilize soil temperature and moisture.
Ensure adequate calcium supply in soil to prevent concurrent blossom-end rot.
Scout lower leaf surfaces weekly for aphid and thrips vectors.
Bell_Pepper___Healthy.treatment_summary: No chemical treatment needed. Maintain optimal plant nutrition and canopy airflow.

Cotton___Bacterial_blight.disease_name: Cotton Bacterial Blight / Angular Leaf Spot (Xanthomonas citri)
preventive_measures: Utilize acid-delinted certified seeds and resistant transgenic cotton varieties.
Plow under infected crop residues immediately following harvest to accelerate decomposition.
Avoid field cultivation and worker transit when foliage is damp from morning dew.
Cotton___Bacterial_blight.treatment_summary: Foliar copper oxychloride sprays can slow progression if applied at early vegetative stages.

preventive_measures: Implement aggressive vector management against sweetpotato whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci).
Eradicate alternate weed hosts (e.g., Sida, Malvaceous weeds) along border canals.
Sow early in the planting window with approved resistant hybrid varieties.
Cotton___Curl_virus.treatment_summary: Viral infections are incurable. Rogue infected plants; apply systemic insecticides for vector suppression.

Cotton___Fusarium_wilt.disease_name: Cotton Fusarium Wilt (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. vasinfectum)
preventive_measures: Implement deep summer plowing to expose fungal resting spores to solar radiation.
Practice 3 to 5 year crop rotation with non-host grass crops like sorghum or corn.
Manage root-knot nematode populations which create entry wounds for Fusarium.
Cotton___Fusarium_wilt.treatment_summary: Treat seed with Trichoderma viride or carbendazim. Remove wilted plants from field.

preventive_measures: Maintain integrated pest management (IPM) monitoring for bollworm and sucking pests.
Provide balanced potash fertilization to strengthen plant cell wall resistance.
Ensure uniform irrigation during square formation and peak boll maturation.
Cotton___Healthy.treatment_summary: No intervention required. Keep vegetative canopies well-ventilated.

preventive_measures: Remove and incinerate all mummified grape clusters and diseased canes during winter pruning.
Train grape canopies on vertical trellises to ensure rapid leaf drying after rain.
Spray protective fungicides starting from early bud swell through 4 weeks post-bloom.
Grape___Black_rot.treatment_summary: Apply kresoxim-methyl, mancozeb, or tebuconazole during critical spring infection windows.

Grape___Esca_Black_Measles.disease_name: Grapevine Esca / Black Measles (Complex Fungal Trunk Disease)
preventive_measures: Protect large pruning wounds immediately with wound sealants or Trichoderma formulations.
Avoid pruning during wet or humid weather when fungal airborne spores are prevalent.
Disinfect pruning shears regularly to prevent vine-to-vine vascular contamination.
Grape___Esca_Black_Measles.treatment_summary: No single chemical cure exists for trunk diseases. Perform trunk renewal or surgical excision.

Grape___Leaf_blight.disease_name: Grape Leaf Blight / Isariopsis Leaf Spot (Pseudocercospora cladosporioides)
preventive_measures: Prune lower lateral leaves around fruiting zones to reduce stagnant humidity.
Collect and compost fallen leaves to eliminate primary inoculum reservoirs.
Maintain optimal vine canopy architecture.
Grape___Leaf_blight.treatment_summary: Foliar sprays of copper hydroxide, azoxystrobin, or difenoconazole give effective control.

preventive_measures: Continue shoot thinning and wire tucking to maximize sun exposure.
Monitor vineyard soil moisture with tensiometers to avoid waterlogging.
Conduct routine scouting for downy mildew and powdery mildew spores.
Grape___Healthy.treatment_summary: Healthy foliage. Follow standard seasonal viticulture protocol.

preventive_measures: Plant corn hybrids with high genetic rust tolerance (Rp gene resistance).
Plant early in the season to evade peak late-summer spore arrival from warm southerly winds.
Scout upper leaves weekly before the silking and tasseling phases.
Maize___Common_rust.treatment_summary: Apply strobilurin or triazole fungicides (e.g. pyraclostrobin + fluxapyroxad) if rust appears before tasseling.

preventive_measures: Practice 1-2 year crop rotation with non-host crops like soybean or clover.
Employ conventional tillage in high-risk zones to bury infected corn residue.
Avoid planting susceptible continuous corn in humid bottomland areas.
Maize___Gray_leaf_spot.treatment_summary: Fungicide application (azoxystrobin or propiconazole) recommended if lesions reach the ear leaf at silking.

preventive_measures: Select corn hybrids possessing Ht-resistance genes.
Rotate infested fields with non-grass crops to allow fungal decomposition.
Bury old crop residue thoroughly via conservation tillage practices.
Maize___Northern_Leaf_Blight.treatment_summary: Apply foliar fungicides (e.g. trifloxystrobin + prothioconazole) when cigar-shaped lesions appear below the ear leaf.

preventive_measures: Maintain balanced nitrogen side-dressing during knee-high (V6) vegetative stage.
Ensure proper plant population density to minimize inter-row competition.
Monitor corn rootworm and armyworm presence during vegetative growth.
Maize___Healthy.treatment_summary: No intervention necessary. Maintain standard agronomic monitoring.

preventive_measures: Maintain adequate plant vigor; avoid nitrogen deficiency which renders plants susceptible.
Use drip or furrow irrigation to minimize foliar wetness periods.
Allow potato tubers to mature fully and skins to set before harvesting.
Potato___Early_blight.treatment_summary: Apply protective chlorothalonil or mancozeb; rotate with boscalid or difenoconazole upon target lesion detection.

preventive_measures: Destroy cull potato piles and volunteer potatoes near fields before planting season.
Plant only certified disease-free seed tubers.
Monitor regional blight forecasting systems during cool, damp weather conditions.
Potato___Late_blight.treatment_summary: Urgent application required: spray cymoxanil, mandipropamid, or metalaxyl immediately upon first signs.

preventive_measures: Hilling rows to ensure proper tuber coverage and prevent greening.
Uniform moisture management to avoid tuber cracking or hollow heart.
Scout field borders for Colorado potato beetles and aphids.
Potato___Healthy.treatment_summary: Healthy foliage. Continue scheduled tuber bulking fertilization.

Rice___Bacterial_leaf_blight.disease_name: Rice Bacterial Leaf Blight (Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae)
preventive_measures: Avoid excessive nitrogenous fertilizer application which fosters succulent susceptible tissues.
Drain standing field water temporarily during severe localized outbreaks.
Adopt resistant cultivars (e.g. varieties with Xa genes) and certified seed.
Rice___Bacterial_leaf_blight.treatment_summary: Spray copper oxychloride + streptomycin sulfate or validamycin at early tillering.

preventive_measures: Correct soil nutrient deficiencies, especially silicon, potassium, and manganese.
Treat seeds with hot water (53-54°C for 10-12 mins) or carbendazim before nursery sowing.
Ensure proper field water retention; avoid severe drought stress in paddy fields.
Rice___Brown_spot.treatment_summary: Foliar spray with propiconazole, iprodione, or tricyclazole at tillering and panicle emergence.

preventive_measures: Avoid high seedling densities in nursery beds; maintain proper row spacing.
Split nitrogen fertilizer into 3-4 split applications rather than heavy early doses.
Maintain continuous shallow flooding (5-10 cm) to suppress airborne spore establishment.
Rice___Leaf_blast.treatment_summary: Spray tricyclazole, isoprothiolane, or kasugamycin immediately upon noticing spindle-shaped lesions.

preventive_measures: Maintain disciplined alternate wetting and drying (AWD) water management.
Perform mid-season drainage to enhance root aeration and tillering strength.
Monitor stem borers and brown planthoppers with pheromone traps.
Rice___Healthy.treatment_summary: Healthy crop. Proceed with routine agronomic care.

preventive_measures: Plant healthy certified setts sourced from disease-free seed cane nurseries.
Subject seed setts to hot-water treatment at 50°C for 2 hours before planting.
Rogue out and burn mosaic-affected stools in the first 45-60 days of sprouting.
Sugarcane___Mosaic.treatment_summary: Incurable viral infection. Suppress aphid vectors (Rhopalosiphum maidis) with recommended systemic insecticides.

preventive_measures: Avoid using setts exhibiting reddish discoloration or fungal pith at node cuttings.
Implement 2-year crop rotation with green manure or paddy rice.
Ensure rapid field drainage during heavy monsoon rains to avoid stagnant root submersion.
Sugarcane___Red_rot.treatment_summary: Dip setts in carbendazim solution (0.1%) before planting; rogue and destroy affected clumps immediately.

preventive_measures: Provide earthing up at 90 and 120 days to support cane lodging resistance.
Trash mulching between rows to conserve moisture and suppress weed emergence.
Maintain balanced micronutrient spraying (zinc, iron) during elongation phase.
Sugarcane___Healthy.treatment_summary: Healthy foliage. Follow standard cane husbandry recommendations.

preventive_measures: Sanitize stakes, cages, and seedling trays with 10% bleach solution before reuse.
Avoid handling or pruning tomato plants while foliage is wet from rain or dew.
Use certified disease-free seeds treated with hydrochloric acid or hot water.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.treatment_summary: Foliar application of copper hydroxide mixed with mancozeb, or actigard systemic acquired resistance inducer.

preventive_measures: Prune bottom 12 inches of foliage once plants are established to prevent soil splash.
Apply 2-3 inches of clean straw or plastic mulch under tomato vines.
Rotate nightshade crops on a minimum 3-year schedule.
Tomato___Early_blight.treatment_summary: Apply biofungicide (Bacillus subtilis) or chemical protectors (chlorothalonil, azoxystrobin) at first concentric ring spot.

preventive_measures: Maintain consistent soil moisture to prevent blossom-end rot and fruit cracking.
Support heavy vines with sturdy staking or Florida weave trellising.
Scout weekly for tomato hornworms, whiteflies, and spider mites.
Tomato___Healthy.treatment_summary: Healthy foliage. Maintain balanced fertilization and consistent drip irrigation.

preventive_measures: Select late blight resistant varieties (e.g. Mountain Magic, Defiant, Plum Regal).
Ensure wide plant spacing (24-36 inches) for maximum aeration and quick drying.
Eliminate volunteer potato and nightshade plants in surrounding field boundaries.
Tomato___Late_blight.treatment_summary: High urgency: apply systemic fungicides (cyazofamid, fluopicolide, or mandipropamid) immediately to prevent total crop loss.

preventive_measures: Ventilate greenhouses and polytunnels actively to keep relative humidity below 85%.
Prune suckers and interior leaves to encourage uniform air circulation.
Water exclusively at soil level using drip emitters; never wet overhead foliage.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.treatment_summary: Apply copper octanoate, difenoconazole, or cyprodinil + fludioxonil upon yellowing on upper leaf surfaces.

preventive_measures: Remove diseased lower leaves as soon as small dark circular spots with gray centers appear.
Thoroughly clean up and compost or burn all tomato vines at season end.
Mulch heavily around the plant base to form a barrier against soil-borne spores.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.treatment_summary: Spray copper fungicides or chlorothalonil on a 7-10 day schedule during wet, warm weather.

preventive_measures: Install 50-mesh insect-proof netting in nursery seedling tunnels to exclude whitefly vectors.
Deploy yellow sticky cards throughout the greenhouse/field to monitor whitefly influx.
Grow TYLCV-resistant hybrids (e.g. Tycoon, Charger, Chef's Choice).
Tomato___Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.treatment_summary: Virus is incurable in plant tissues. Immediately rogue out and bag infected plants. Control whitefly populations.

preventive_measures: Sow certified rust-resistant wheat varieties recommended for your agro-ecological zone.
Eradicate volunteer wheat plants in fall which serve as a 'green bridge' for spores.
Avoid late sowing which exposes wheat to higher spring temperatures and heavy spore loads.
Wheat___Brown_rust.treatment_summary: Apply propiconazole, tebuconazole, or azoxystrobin when flag leaf rust pustules exceed 1-2% severity.

preventive_measures: Ensure balanced basal fertilization and timely crown root initiation (CRI) irrigation.
Maintain weed-free conditions during early tillering.
Scout for aphids and cereal leaf beetles.
Wheat___Healthy.treatment_summary: Healthy foliage. Follow recommended regional irrigation schedule.

preventive_measures: Practice minimum 1-year rotation away from wheat to break residue-borne pycnidia cycle.
Select wheat cultivars with high resistance ratings against Septoria tritici.
Delay autumn sowing slightly in regions with severe endemic Septoria history.
Wheat___Septoria.treatment_summary: Apply multi-site protective fungicides (folpet) mixed with SDHI/triazole (fluxapyroxad or mefentrifluconazole) at GS 39.

preventive_measures: Monitor fields early in cool spring weather (10-15°C) for characteristic yellow stripe patterns.
Plant genetically diverse seed mixtures or multi-line resistant cultivars.
Destroy collateral volunteer grass hosts along field headlands.
Wheat___Yellow_rust.treatment_summary: High urgency: apply propiconazole or pyraclostrobin immediately upon noticing bright yellow stripe pustules.
